page: Microsoft Azure FX8-4ms_v2 is a high-frequency, memory-intensive virtual machine built on dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processors. Operating at a base clock frequency of 4.2 GHz, the instance provisions 2 physical cores and 4 dedicated vCPUs on the x86_64 architecture under Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. The CPU subsystem features a 260 MB L3 cache alongside advanced vector capabilities, including AVX-512, AMX-tile, and AMX-INT8 instructions. Backing this compute engine is an expansive memory allocation of 168.0 GB of RAM, resulting in an exceptionally dense 42.0 GB per vCPU. The server type includes no bundled local ephemeral storage and features no discrete GPU hardware.

Benchmark measurements highlight strong single-threaded performance driven by the 4.2 GHz clock rate. Geekbench single-core evaluations place the instance in the top 10% with a score of 2351.0, mirrored by top-quartile performance in single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression. In contrast, parallel multi-core throughput is constrained by the physical core count of two, placing multi-threaded stress-ng and bzip3 benchmarks in the bottom quartile. Uncached memory bandwidth for large blocks remains modest at 36.1 GB/sec for reads and 25.44 GB/sec for writes.

From a qualitative efficiency perspective, the FX8-4ms_v2 optimizes software licensing economics by delivering a massive memory capacity per licensed core alongside high per-thread compute velocity. This configuration provides a focused architecture for memory-resident databases, in-memory caching solutions, electronic design automation (EDA), and financial modeling applications where workload demands hinge on single-thread execution speed and high memory density rather than high core counts.
description: Microsoft Azure FX8-4ms_v2 is a memory-dense, compute-oriented instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture with Microsoft Hyper-V, it provides 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores, accompanied by a 260 MB L3 cache and support for AVX-512 and AMX instruction sets. With an expansive 168.0 GB of RAM—yielding 42.0 GB per vCPU—it pairs significant in-memory capacity with top-tier single-core CPU execution, achieving upper-decile single-core benchmark scores alongside strong single-threaded compression throughput. The instance includes no onboard local storage and lacks discrete GPUs, relying on remote persistent storage. Constrained parallel scaling reflects its low core count, resulting in lower multi-core benchmark rankings. Qualitatively, the server provides high efficiency for memory-heavy, single-thread-sensitive workloads where core count is intentionally restricted to manage per-core licensing expenses, making it suitable for specialized in-memory relational databases, electronic design automation, and caching layers.
